title: Second total-filtration images equal truncation images
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be left exact additive functors between Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories satisfying injective acyclicity [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. For every presentation $P$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], let $L_P$ be a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] of $\operatorname{Tot}G(I_P)$ whose degreewise steps are the second total filtration [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Suppose total-cohomology isomorphisms $h_P^n$ are normalized by the common augmentation and the canonical injective-resolution computation. For every $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $n\ge0$, the image of $H^n(L_P^p)\to H^n(\operatorname{Tot}G(I_P))\xrightarrow{h_P^n}R^n(GF)(P.X)$ equals the canonical transport of the truncation spectral-object imageFiltration step at $n+1-p$.

source.place: Tag 015X, second spectral sequence and filtered CE injective resolutions; Tag 015N

proof.text: For q=n-p, cycles of Dec(L)^(-q) in degree n are precisely total cycles lying in L^p; the extra differential condition is automatic on cycles. Hence both complexes have the same image in full cohomology.

Horizontal cycle, boundary and homology resolutions make Dec(Tot(I)) a filtered injective resolution of the canonical truncation filtration of F(J). Injective terms split degreewise filtrations, and left exact additive G preserves the kernels and finite sums defining Dec. The filtered computation of Tag 015X identifies the piece with RG(tau_{<=q} F(J)), compatibly with the full object. Augmentation normalization fixes the full-object comparison. Taking images gives the equality. For p<0 both images are whole; for p>n both are zero.
